title: Nextiva Review (2026)
intro: Nextiva is evaluated here as a cloud business phone system — Nextiva is a cloud business phone and customer-communications platform aimed at SMBs. Published annual floors (verified 2026-08-17): Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/month ($23/$50 monthly on Core/Engage). Contact Center Essential starts from $75/agent. Recording is an add-on on Core; analytics and AI land on higher plans / XBert add-on from $99/mo. Annual SMB pricing commonly targets new customers with 1–100 employees on 12-month+ terms. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s business-communications methodology (ease of use, voice/messaging quality, routing and workflows, integrations, analytics, outbound tools, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Nextiva when you want a transparent SMB cloud-phone floor with messaging apps (including WhatsApp) and a path into contact centre without jumping straight to enterprise UCaaS quotes.
verdict: Choose Nextiva when you want a transparent SMB cloud-phone floor with messaging apps (including WhatsApp) and a path into contact centre without jumping straight to enterprise UCaaS quotes. Compare Aircall for CRM/CTI depth, RingCentral for enterprise UCaaS scale, Dialpad for included call AI, and CallHippo for lower-friction SMB entry experiments. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, minimums and usage rates on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Nextiva markets a straightforward SMB phone-and-messaging setup with published plan names (Core/Engage/Scale). Score reflects documented packaging clarity, not hands-on lab testing.
Cloud phone plus SMS, WhatsApp/messaging apps, team messaging and video give Nextiva a broad multi-channel envelope for SMB customer communications.
Business call routing covers typical SMB PBX needs; contact-centre Essential/Professional deepen queues and dialer workflows as a separate ladder rather than Core defaults.
Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk, Slack, Teams and Google Workspace connectors are present; CTI depth is often add-on packaged, which caps the integrations score below CTI specialists.
Reporting strengthens on higher plans — scored as capable but higher-plan gated relative to Dialpad’s included AI analytics posture.
SMS and calling cover standard outbound; power dialer requires contact-centre Professional. Adequate for SMB outbound, not dialer-first sales teams on Core.
Core → Engage → Scale plus Contact Center Essential from $75/agent covers growth into mid-market, with eligibility constraints on promotional SMB annual pricing.

Core at $15/user/month annual with high-confidence first-party verification is one of the clearest SMB phone floors in this set; Engage at $25 remains accessible before Scale/CC/AI add-ons raise TCO. Affiliate economics excluded.
AI on Scale and XBert from $99/mo are real but higher-plan/add-on packaged — credible AI without Dialpad’s included-on-entry advantage.

faq.question: Is Nextiva a business phone system?
faq.answer: Yes. Nextiva is a cloud business phone system: virtual numbers, inbound and outbound calling, softphone apps and call routing. It is not a CRM of record — keep your CRM and connect it for call logging.

faq.question: How is Nextiva priced?
faq.answer: Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/mo annual ($23/$50 monthly for Core/Engage). Contact Center Essential from $75/agent. Recording add-on on Core; AI on Scale / XBert from $99/mo. Verified high confidence 2026-08-17 on nextiva.com/nextiva-pricing — confirm SMB eligibility (often 1–100 employees, 12-month+) live.

faq.question: Does Nextiva have a free plan or free trial?
faq.answer: No free plan is published. A free trial is documented. Confirm current terms with the vendor.

faq.question: Did SoftwareGlimpse personally test Nextiva?
faq.answer: No. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research evidence, not hands-on product usage. Affiliate relationships never influence scores.
